facts.text: La Traviata premiered on 6 March 1853 at La Fenice in Venice.
facts.evidence: It was first performed on 6 March 1853 at La Fenice opera house in Venice.

facts.text: The day after the premiere, Verdi wrote his most famous letter: “La traviata last night a failure. Was the fault mine or the singers’? Time will tell.”
facts.attribution: Verdi, letter to Emanuele Muzio, 1853 (via Wikipedia)
facts.evidence: La traviata last night a failure. Was the fault mine or the singers'? Time will tell.

facts.text: The premiere audience jeered at times, some of it aimed at the casting of Fanny Salvini-Donatelli as Violetta.
facts.evidence: The audience jeered at times during the premiere, directing some of their scorn at the casting of soprano Fanny Salvini-Donatelli

facts.text: Revised and revived in 1854, it was a hit. Piave reported: “Then it was a fiasco; now it has created a furore. Draw your own conclusions!”
evidence: it was a fiasco; now it has created a furore. Draw your own conclusions!

facts.text: Verdi wanted a contemporary setting, but La Fenice insisted on the past (“c. 1700”). Realistic modern-dress productions came only in the 1880s.
evidence: the authorities at La Fenice insisted that it be set in the past, "c. 1700"

facts.text: The story comes from La Dame aux camélias by Alexandre Dumas fils, which Verdi saw in Paris with Giuseppina Strepponi in 1852.
evidence: It is based on La Dame aux camélias (1852), a play by Alexandre Dumas fils
In February the couple attended a performance of Alexander Dumas fils'  The Lady of the Camellias.

facts.text: By coincidence, an Italian translation of the Dumas play was running just down the street from La Fenice at the premiere.
facts.evidence: an Italian translation of the play La Dame aux camélias was being presented just a short distance from La Fenice

facts.text: Verdi told Piave he wanted something new: “I don’t want any of those everyday subjects that one can find by the hundreds.”
facts.evidence: I don't want any of those everyday subjects that one can find by the hundreds.

facts.text: Verdi arrived in Venice for rehearsals “filled with premonitions of disaster” and made his unhappiness clear to the singers.
facts.evidence: Verdi was filled with premonitions of disaster upon his arrival in Venice on 21 February for rehearsals

facts.text: The prelude opens with very soft, very high strings portraying the frail heroine, then the main love theme on lower strings.
facts.evidence: The prelude to the opera begins with very soft, very high strings depicting the frail heroine

facts.text: Asked for a toast, Alfredo sings the brindisi “Libiamo ne’ lieti calici”, “Let’s drink from the joyful cups”.
After the Brindisi, an offstage band plays waltzes. Waltz rhythms run through Act I to create a Parisian atmosphere.
facts.evidence: waltz rhythms pervade the first act of the opera, creating a Parisian atmosphere

facts.text: The long Germont–Violetta duet is built in many sections, the music following each turn of the drama.
facts.evidence: is multi-sectioned with the music following the changing dramatic situation

facts.text: “Di Provenza il mar, il suol”: Germont tries to comfort his son by reminding him of home in Provence.
facts.evidence: attempts to comfort his son, reminding him of his family in Provence

facts.text: At Flora’s party, guests dress up as gypsy girls and matadors from Madrid to entertain.
facts.evidence: Noi siamo zingarelle venute da lontano

facts.text: In New York, diarist George Templeton Strong shrugged at the scandal: the plot was no worse than Don Giovanni, which on stage was “little but rampant lechery”.
facts.evidence: which as put on the stage is little but rampant lechery

facts.text: La Traviata is among the most frequently performed of all operas.
facts.evidence: is among the most frequently performed of all operas
